{{Quote|Freia lures the Neimoidians to Imynusoph, whose natives seem peaceable, though Freia has become rather high-handed in her dealings ''[&hellip;]''. Thoax and Farge are eager to stake their claim on to this purported treasure world (Thoax and Farge: "The Vaults of Imynusoph"), and are horrified when Freia reveals herself at a banquet in a great temple ''[&hellip;]''<nowiki></nowiki>|Excerpts from the program for the [[2 ABY/Legends|38:2:13]] premiere of ''The Kallea Cycle''|<ref name="TEA" />}}
'''Imynusoph''' was an [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim Territories]] [[Planet/Legends|world]] that, according to the [[Opera/Legends|opera]] ''[[The Kallea Cycle]]'', was the site of rumored treasures around [[3694 BBY]], when the [[Hyperspace/Legends|hyperspace]] [[Scout/Legends|scout]] [[Freia Kallea/Legends|Freia Kallea]] charted the [[Hydian Spur|final segment]] of the [[Super-hyperroute/Legends|super-hyperroute]] that would become known as the [[Hydian Way/Legends|Hydian Way]]. In the [[Music/Legends|opera]], Imynusoph was the [[Homeworld/Legends|homeworld]] of the peaceful [[Imyni/Legends|Imyni]] [[Species/Legends|species]].

The opera depicted the attempt by Kallea to capture her rivals [[Thoax Osaax|Thoax]] and [[Farge Osaax]] in the [[Temple of Imynusoph]], with her plans waylaid by the betrayal of the Imyni and the arrival of reinforcements for both the scout's and the Osaaxes's side of the confrontation. In the opera's climax, a battle ensued between the parties present on Imynusoph, which led to the [[Death/Legends|death]] of Kallea's fellow scout, [[Banu Hydia]].

Nearly four [[Millennium/Legends|millennia]] after Kallea extended the Hydian Way to Imynusoph, the latter remained outside of the borders of [[The galaxy/Legends|galactic]] governments but was considered part of the [[Kallea sector/Legends|Kallea sector]] by [[0 ABY/Legends|0 ABY]].

==Description==
Imynusoph was a [[Planet/Legends|world]] located within the [[Star system/Legends|star system]] of the [[Imynusoph system/Legends|same name]], which was part of the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim Territories']]<ref name="TEA" /> [[Kallea sector/Legends|Kallea sector]].<ref name="EAOC" />

==History==
In [[3694 BBY]], the [[Human/Legends|Human]] [[Hyperspace/Legends|hyperspace]] [[Scout/Legends|scout]] [[Freia Kallea/Legends|Freia Kallea]] extended a [[Hyperspace route/Legends|hyperlane]] she had previously blazed that connected the [[Rimma Trade Route/Legends|Rimma Trade Route]] with the [[Terminus system/Legends|Terminus system]]. Kallea charted a new route, which would eventually be named the [[Hydian Spur]], from [[Terminus/Legends|Terminus]] to Imynusoph. The Hydian Spur went on to become the final segment of the [[Hydian Way/Legends|Hydian Way]] [[Super-hyperroute/Legends|super-hyperroute]] stretching across the entire [[The galaxy/Legends|galaxy]].<ref name="TEA" />

The area of [[Realspace/Legends|space]] surrounding Imynusoph had been explored by [[3000 BBY]]. During the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]], the Outer Rim world fell outside the borders of the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]],<ref name="TEA" /> and remained outside the sphere of influence of the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]] by [[17 BBY/Legends|17 BBY]],<ref name="TEGTW">''[[The Essential Guide to Warfare]]''</ref> although it became incorporated as part of the Empire's Kallea [[Sector/Legends|sector]] by [[0 ABY/Legends|0 ABY]].<ref name="EAOC" /> Around [[25 ABY/Legends|25 ABY]], the population of the Imynusoph system numbered less than one million.<ref name="TEA" />

===''The Kallea Cycle''===
{{Quote|<nowiki></nowiki>''[&hellip;]'' even as the Neimoidians summon a band of Gran and Dug thugs they've brought for protection&mdash;and Sival Brentioch ''[&hellip;]'' arrives with a fleet from Brentaal. In the battle that follows, Banu saves Freia but is mortally wounded.|Excerpts from the program for the [[2 ABY/Legends|38:2:13]] premiere of ''The Kallea Cycle''|<ref name="TEA" />}}
Twenty-two [[Standard century/Legends|hundred]] [[Standard year/Legends|years]] after Kallea blazed the Hydian Way, the [[Musician/Legends|composer]] [[Trebian Shullos]] wrote ''[[The Kallea Cycle]]'', an [[Opera/Legends|opera]] that depicted how the resolute scout overcame the difficulties in charting the extensive hyperlane. The climax of the third and final act of the [[Music/Legends|opera]], which was titled "The [[Temple of Imynusoph]]," took place on Imynusoph, which in the musical composition was depicted as a rumored treasure world.<ref name="TEA" />

[[File:The_Kallea_Cycle.jpg|thumb|right|200px|Imynusoph was the setting of the climax in the opera ''The Kallea Cycle''.]]
In the opera, Kallea attempted to exact revenge on her rivals [[Thoax Osaax|Thoax]] and [[Farge Osaax]] by setting a trap for them on Imynusoph. The Human scout lured the two [[Neimoidian/Legends|Neimoidians]], who were eager to claim the purported riches of Imynusoph&mdash;as represented by the aria "[[The Vaults of Imynusoph]]"&mdash;to a great temple there. To the horror of the Osaaxes, Kallea revealed herself at a banquet at the temple and ordered the native [[Imyni/Legends|Imyni]] to bind the Neimoidians.<ref name="TEA" />

However, the natives chose that moment to turn on all the offworlders as a result of Kallea's high-handed attitude. At the same [[Time/Legends|time]], a band of [[Dug/Legends|Dug]] and [[Gran/Legends|Gran]] [[Mercenary/Legends|thugs]] hired by the Neimoidians for protection arrived on Imynusoph, and so did a [[Fleet/Legends|fleet]] led by Kallea's secret admirer and patron, [[Sival Brentioch]], whom the scout knew only by the name "Arhul Habea."<ref name="TEA" />

During the climactic [[Battle on Imynusoph|battle]] that ensued, the temple was set [[Fire/Legends|ablaze]], and Kallea was saved by her fellow scout, the [[Duros/Legends|Duros]] [[Banu Hydia]], at the cost of his own life. As Hydia lay [[Death/Legends|dying]], Brentioch revealed to Kallea his true identity as well as his feelings for the scout and his patronage of her trailblazing work. In the opera's denouement, the Osaaxes were arrested, and Kallea and Brentioch left Imynusoph, taking Hydia's body with them for [[Burial/Legends|burial]] on their [[Homeworld/Legends|native world]], [[Brentaal IV/Legends|Brentaal]].<ref name="TEA" />

==Inhabitants==
{{Quote|Freia orders the Imyni to bind the Neimoidians, but the Imyni turn on all the outworlders ''[&hellip;]''<nowiki></nowiki>|Excerpts from the program for the 38:2:13 premiere of ''The Kallea Cycle''|<ref name="TEA" />}}
In the opera ''The Kallea Cycle'', Imynusoph was depicted as home to the [[Sentience/Legends|sentient]] Imyni [[Species/Legends|species]]. The Imyni were portrayed as being peaceful people when offworlders first arrived on Imynusoph, but Freia Kallea's inconsiderate behavior led the natives to revolt against all the foreign visitors that had arrived on their world.<ref name="TEA" />

==Locations==
{{Quote|As he ''[Banu Hydia]'' lies dying in the burning temple, Sival reveals his true identity and his role as Freia's benefactor ''[&hellip;]''<nowiki></nowiki>|Excerpts from the program for the 38:2:13 premiere of ''The Kallea Cycle''|<ref name="TEA" />}}
Imynusoph was portrayed in the opera ''The Kallea Cycle'' as the site of a great structure known as the Temple of Imynusoph. In the composition, Freia Kallea attempted to capture her rivals Thoax and Farge Osaax during a banquet in the temple. Her plans went awry due to an insurgence by the local Imyni people as well as the arrival of other parties connected to Kallea and the Osaaxes, and the temple was set ablaze during the ensuing confrontation.<ref name="TEA" />

==Behind the scenes==
Imynusoph was introduced via mention of the Temple of Imynusoph in the "[[Galaxywide NewsNets]]" feature of [[West End Games]]' [[Star Wars Adventure Journal 13|''Star Wars Adventure Journal'' 13]], which was published in [[May]] [[1997]]. The feature was authored by [[Peter M. Schweighofer|Peter Schweighofer]].<ref name="GNN">{{JournalCite|13|Galaxywide NewsNets}}</ref>

The [[2009]] reference book ''[[The Essential Atlas]]'', authored by [[Daniel Wallace]] and [[Jason Fry]], identified Imynusoph as a world and placed it in grid square J-21.<ref name="TEA" /> Fry has [[:File:JasonFryAtlas.png|stated]] that the star systems listed in Appendix section of ''The Essential Atlas'' are named after the most prominent planets or celestial bodies located in those systems. This article therefore considers the Imynusoph system to be named after the planet Imynusoph, which is assumed to have existed in the ''[[Star Wars]]'' [[Galaxy/Legends|galaxy]] independently of its [[in-universe]] depiction in ''The Kallea Cycle''.
